html:
The system of armed convoys that carried goods between Spain and its American empire from 1566 to 1790, and above all carried American silver home. It was run from Seville, later Cádiz, by the Casa de Contratación (House of Trade).

Each year two fleets sailed from Spain:

  • the flota to Veracruz in Mexico
  • the galeones to Cartagena and to the isthmus of Panama, where the silver of Potosí and Peru was brought overland

Both then met at Havana and sailed home together, guarded by warships. In the Pacific the Manila galleons linked Mexico to Asia.

The convoys made Spanish silver the money of the world, and they drew pirates and enemy navies. Few were ever taken whole; the Dutch captured one in 1628, and hurricanes sank others, such as the fleet of 1715 off Florida. As Spain opened trade to more ports in the 1700s, the system faded out.
sum: The system of armed convoys that carried goods between Spain and its American empire from 1566 to 1790, and above all carried American silver home. It was run from Seville, later Cádiz, by the Casa de Contratación (House of Trade).
